per_window.ps-ns: search_insufficient for the entry construct (MIA40-J2). No row reports MIA40 relaxation; the 2009 structure paper, read only as an abstract, calls the N-terminal lid rigid without naming the probe or window (J1, r1, full-length construct).
per_window.us-ms: search_insufficient (J3). No dispersion or exchange measurement of MIA40 exists in any redox or binding state; CPMG and relaxation in the ALR papers concern ALR.
per_window.undetermined: Substrate- and partner-bound states, each a bound-state comparison without a MIA40 rate: trapped C53S complexes with Cox17 (secondary structure unchanged, CPC and cleft perturbed; J5, r2), the Tim9 ITS peptide (J6, r3) and CRAC sf-ALR (J9, r6, r7). Reduced-CPC MIA40 is oxidised by long-form ALR and partly by short-form ALR at 298 K, redox chemistry rather than conformational exchange (J7, J8; r4, r5). The N-terminal AIF-interaction region shields the active site in the inactive SPS background: its removal or the AIA-A mutation shifts active-site and core aromatic resonances (F68, F72, F91) and extends the SAXS shape (J10-J12; r9-r11), and a SAXS-restrained MD ensemble of an AIF fusion allows an unengaged N-terminal fragment (J13, r12, md_only). Artefact lead: the redox-active truncated core forms persistent intermolecular disulfides (J14, r13). Not judged: in-cell and in-mitochondria NMR of the redox state (r8, r14, abstracts), MitoBloCK negative-control titrations (r15) and ITC binding to mutant AIF (r16).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Not measured: for the free, oxidised MIA40 folded domain (UniProt 41-106) no row reports relaxation, dispersion or exchange broadening, so neither µs-ms exchange nor its absence is shown; the 2009 structure paper, read only as an abstract, calls the N-terminal lid rigid without a stated method or window.
questions_for_gina: The input card gives no BMRB id; is the RelaxDB MIA40 set the folded-domain part (41-106) of a full-length MIA40 relaxation measurement from Banci et al. 2009 (2K3J), and in which CPC redox state?

Should the bound-state chemical-shift maps (Cox17, Tim9 peptide, ALR adducts) and the SPS/AIA-A construct comparisons be counted as alternate-state evidence at all, given that none measures a MIA40 rate?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The measured samples differ from the entry in construct (full length with GSFT, C53S trapping mutant, C53S/C55S SPS, AIA-A, ΔN, AIF fusion), redox state (reduced versus oxidised CPC) and binding state, so no row describes the entry reference state. Buffers are phosphate/EDTA (2010, 2011 papers) or HEPES with 5 mM TCEP (2025 paper); TCEP keeps SPS samples reduced at non-structural cysteines. Several residue maps are figure-only, so only author-named residues are listed.
